mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains below its last-month average, commuting-linked foot traffic stays suppressed and RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks. The signal acts through reduced weekday errands and lower spontaneous shopping tied to office travel.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES does not recover by at least 5 points from t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: A weekly rebound in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent trough indicates renewed out-of-home errand behavior that spills into convenience shopping and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks. The effect is strongest when GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT move up together.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 3 points week-on-week from a prior decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after a 3+ point weekly rise in GROCERY_PHARM, or rises only when TRANSIT is flat or falling.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls sharply relative to the prior week, retail access weakens immediately and RETAIL_REC declines over the next week. This is a short-horizon mobility-disruption signal because lower station usage directly reduces shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: After a TRANSIT drop of 5 or more points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC fails to fall in the following week in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS together with RESIDENTIAL indicates time shifting toward local outdoor and home-based activity, which crowds out discretionary retail visits and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism is seasonal because it reflects substitution away from shopping trips rather than commuting.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days when PARKS is above its recent mean and RESIDENTIAL is simultaneously elevated.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rebound from their recent lows, weekday mobility normalizes and RETAIL_REC increases within four weeks. The joint movement matters because office reactivation without transit recovery does not deliver enough customer flow to retail corridors.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise at least 4 points from the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 28 days despite simultaneous 4+ point weekly gains in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while GROCERY_PHARM stays below its baseline, households are substituting toward home-centered routines and fewer discretionary trips, which depresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The effect should appear even without changes in workplaces.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays at least 15 points above baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains 15+ points above baseline and GROCERY_PHARM does not strengthen.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in TRANSIT below the recent average signals renewed access friction or behavioral avoidance, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The claim fails if transit falls but retail does not weaken, because then the mobility restriction channel is not transmitting.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT is below its prior 4-week mean by at least 3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its last 28-day mean during periods when TRANSIT is at least 3 points below its prior 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday-shopping regime, simultaneous improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates more out-of-home activity and broader trip chaining, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next week. The short horizon reflects immediate discretionary spending responses rather than slow commuting effects.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week when both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS rise together from the prior week.
